origin.description: The old name of str_view. It warns and then shows the strings.
origin.usage: str_view_all(string, pattern = NULL, match = NA, html = FALSE, use_escapes = FALSE)

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector. A missing string stays missing.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression, or a fixed, coll, or boundary modifier. NULL only marks unusual whitespace.

arguments.name: match
arguments.text: NA, the default, keeps every element. TRUE keeps matches. FALSE keeps the others.

arguments.name: html
arguments.text: TRUE would build an HTML widget. That needs htmltools and htmlwidgets, which are not installed here.

arguments.name: use_escapes
arguments.text: TRUE renders non-ASCII and non-printable characters as unicode escapes.

origin.details: Deprecated in stringr 1.5.0 in favour of str_view. The default match is NA, so elements that do not match are still shown. The text view is the same as str_view.
origin.value: A character vector of the highlighted strings, with the original positions kept as an index.

translation.description: The old name of str_view. It warns and then shows the strings.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings. A missing string is stringi NA.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression, or a fixed, coll, or boundary modifier. None only marks unusual whitespace.

arguments.name: match
arguments.text: NA, the default, keeps every element. True keeps matches. False keeps the others.

arguments.name: html
arguments.text: True is refused. htmltools and htmlwidgets are not a dependency.

arguments.name: use_escapes
arguments.text: True renders non-ASCII and non-printable characters as unicode escapes.

translation.details: Calls lifecycle.deprecate_warn for stringr 1.5.0, then str_view. The default match is NA, so a string that does not match is still returned.
translation.value: A list of highlighted strings. ids are the 1-based input positions. spans are the match locations.
